contract.description: SDK contract version range, fixed grammar (sdk-contract-v1.md §2.1, decided 2026-08-07): exactly one comparator pair `>=A.B,<C.D`, no whitespace, bounds MAJOR.MINOR.

isolation_mode.description: §2.1 (ADR-0018): `shared` is the only value in v1 - one container instance per minigame per event, started at event bootstrap, shared by all teams, decommissioned at event end; the framework provisions each team's players onto the running instance at challenge start and removes them at teardown. Sharing is safe because a minigame must never grant a player root: an escalation game's target is that team's own service account (svc-<team_handle>), never root and never one service account shared by all teams. That rule, and the hardening obligations that go with it, are verified by registry admission review and the contract test suite, not by this schema. The field is kept although it has one legal value, so that a per-team instance mode can be added post-v1 as a new enum value without a schema_version bump; a manifest declaring anything else is rejected today.

provision_identity.description: §2.1: `handles` = /provision carries opaque ids and framework-generated handles only. `names` = the game additionally receives team_name, players[].username and players[].display_name; declaring it is a stated data-processing capability - justified in the registry submission, visible in the event's privacy notice, covered by teardown/logging tests (ADR-0019).

solve_mode.description: §2.1/§5: how a solve reaches the framework. `flag` = the game displays a produced `token` reward and the player submits it in the framework UI, so the solver is identified. `callback` = the game detects the win itself and calls the solved callback; use it only when there is nothing to paste. A manifest declaring a non-empty tcp_ports must use `flag` (§3.4 check 11).

produces.description: at most one slot of type `token` - a minigame has one flag or none (§2.1, the schema half of §3.4 check 12); holds for callback games too

ociImageRef.description: OCI image reference (§2.1): [registry[:port]/]path[/path...][:tag][@digest]. Path components are lowercase per the OCI distribution grammar; the registry host, tag and digest are all optional.
